title: A retry decorator with arguments
problem: Network calls fail now and then. Write retry(times, exceptions=(Exception,)), a decorator factory: @retry(3, exceptions=(ConnectionError,)) makes a function try again when it raises one of the listed exceptions, up to `times` calls in total, and re-raise the last error if every attempt fails. Other exceptions must not be retried, and the decorated function must keep its name and docstring.
requirements: retry(times, exceptions) returns a decorator; the decorator returns a wrapper that accepts any positional and keyword arguments and passes them on
The wrapped function is called at most `times` times per call of the wrapper; the first successful result is returned
Only exceptions that are instances of one of `exceptions` (subclasses included) are retried; any other exception propagates immediately
When the last attempt fails, the last exception itself is re-raised (not a new one)
retry(0) or a negative number raises ValueError right away, when retry(...) is called
Use functools.wraps so __name__, __doc__ and __wrapped__ refer to the original function
No sleeping or backoff (keep the tests fast)
contract: retry(times: int, exceptions: tuple[type[BaseException], ...] = (Exception,)) -> Callable[[F], F]
expectedBehavior: A function that fails twice with ConnectionError and then returns 'ok', decorated with @retry(3), returns 'ok' after 3 calls; with @retry(2) it raises the second ConnectionError after 2 calls.
edgeCases: times < 1: ValueError when retry(...) is called
An exception type that isn't listed: no retry
A subclass of a listed exception: retried
Each call of the decorated function starts again with `times` attempts
hints: Conceptual: there are three layers. retry(...) receives the settings, the decorator receives the function, and the wrapper runs on every call. Validation of `times` belongs to the outer layer because it must happen when retry(...) is called.

Specific: `except exceptions:` accepts a tuple of exception types and matches subclasses. Keep the attempt counter local to the wrapper (a loop variable), not in an outer scope, so every call starts fresh. A bare `raise` inside except re-raises the current exception unchanged.

Implementation: in the wrapper, loop attempt over 1..times; inside, try to return func(*args, **kwargs); in `except exceptions:`, re-raise if this was the last attempt, otherwise let the loop continue.
evaluation: Unlisted exceptions are not caught at all (no catching everything and filtering by hand)
